Root mode runs the engine as root. It can damage the current runtime environment and lose session or workspace data.\n\nContinue?
This mode is extremely dangerous — the engine can read and write every file outside the sandbox.\n\nTurn on Root mode?

Root mode is on. Do not edit, move, or delete files inside the app directories (files/engine, files/dsh-home) or the workspace folder.

Files written there by a root process are owned by root with restrictive permissions. The app then cannot read them, and the symptoms look like 'plugin failed to load' or 'engine will not start' - usually only fixable by clearing app data.

Keep your own files (documents, code, projects) in an outside folder such as Documents/ and let the agent work there.

If you must change something inside the app directories, use the app's own settings or plugins instead of a root file manager.

DSH Mobile is a local engine shell for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) on Android: it runs the full Node.js agent engine inside the phone\'s sandbox — no server needed, and your sessions stay on the device. Only model requests go out, to whichever API endpoint you configure.
Built on the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) agent framework, open-sourced by DeepSeek in Aug 2026

System-level recognizer. Local inference via sherpa-onnx, models from a China-reachable mirror. No desktop icon - open it from here.

Tap the entry above to open the GitHub Releases page in your browser, then download the latest dsh-asr-service arm64-v8a APK (about 31 MB). Install it and allow installation from your browser when prompted. It will not add an icon to your home screen.
2. Open it and download a model

Open it from this page (the entry above) or from the system Voice input settings. Go to Models and download one. zipformer-zh-14m-int8 is small and fast - good to start with. Pick paraformer-zh-int8 if you want better accuracy and have space. Models stay on your device; the download source follows your system language (HuggingFace official for English, a China-reachable mirror for Chinese) and can be overridden in the app settings.

Inside the app, tap Set as system default. It needs Shizuku or root; without either, go to Settings - Languages & input - Voice input and pick the app there. On ROMs that redirect that page, you can instead choose it directly here in DSH Mobile (see the Recognition engine setting).

Go back to Voice services - Speech recognition and set Recognition engine to the DSH offline recognizer. Then tap the floating microphone: recognition now runs fully offline. Tap Run check inside the recognizer app any time to verify every step.

No icon after install: expected - it is a service plugin, open it from this page. Model download fails: check the network, the mirror is hf-mirror.com. Voice input still uses the wrong engine: set it explicitly under Recognition engine. Recognition returns nothing: run Run check in the app, it names the missing step.

Install our offline speech recognizer for the system
Android only offers speech recognition if the device has a recognizer installed. Many phones (especially Chinese ROMs) ship without one, so voice input fails outright.

A) Install a local recognizer app — it registers as a system recognition service, and this app uses it automatically. Nothing to fill in here. Recommended (all verified to declare android.speech.RecognitionService):
· Sayboard (Vosk) — github.com/ElishaAz/Sayboard F-Droid, active. Import vosk-model-cn-0.22 (~1.3GB) for much better Chinese.
· whisperIME — github.com/woheller69/whisperIME F-Droid, active. Multilingual Whisper (~435MB), good Chinese.
· whisperIMEplus — github.com/woheller69/whisperIMEplus Faster ONNX version, updated more often.
Then pick it under Settings > System > Languages & input > Voice input.

B) Use a cloud ASR service — paste its OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, model name and API key below. Providers with free tiers: SiliconFlow (siliconflow.cn), Groq (groq.com), Alibaba DashScope, Zhipu BigModel, Volcengine Ark, or your own server (whisper.cpp).
